title: A worker briefed for STORE-level work edited ssot/build_tabbed.py, the corpus build entry point
detail: Brief said: fix at the generator IF a class exists, at the store if not, and never edit a *_REVIEW.html. It did not say 'do not touch the build entry point', and the worker read a genuine class defect (an empty table with a caption promising per-trial rows) and fixed it there. It planted all five results TRUE -- but only on IV_IRON_HF. Measured after: the edit changes behaviour on 15 objects, all of which DO hold a remainder screen, under topic-specific keys (ablation_hf_2026_08_19, iv_iron_2026_08_19, adjudication, unscreened_remainder). A plant on one page does not measure a class change. REVERTED.
ask: The brief needs a rule the worker could have followed: name the files that are class-wide, and require a blast-radius count before any edit to one. 'Fix at the generator' and 'do not make an unmeasured class change' are in tension as written.

title: The suppressed-screening-table fix is real but needs its own gated pass over 15 objects
detail: IV_IRON_HF renders Table 61 'Every trial, with its reason' as em dashes -- '- screened, - included, - excluded, - not-assessable, k after screening: -'. The worker's fix suppresses the table and states why, which is derive-or-refuse done correctly. But 15 objects take that path and each currently renders SOMETHING; suppression removes it. Whether that is an improvement depends on whether the other 14 render real content or dashes, which nobody has measured.
ask: Route to a lane that can measure all 15 before/after and plant on more than one. The reverted patch is recoverable from this session; it is not lost.

title: A rendered store needs a declared NON-RENDERED namespace, or every future *_was is a coin flip
detail: Measured at origin/main e3a9c964b: 2,074 private-named fields across 155 objects; 454 values appear in served bytes; 446 of those are _note fields that are reader-facing BY DESIGN; 8 are *_was; of those 8, 7 are coincidence (the text also lives in outcomes/name, definition or introduction) and 1 (arni-hfref) renders correctly as 'Previously third-party convergent inference' with an upgrade timestamp. So ZERO defects today -- but 92 *_was fields exist and any could leak. The only leak tonight was one I created and removed.
ask: Declare a prefix the projector never renders (e.g. leading underscore, or a reserved _audit block), and make the generator assert it. Convention alone will be broken by the next person in a hurry, and it fails silently.

title: colchicine-pericarditis evidence is RECOVERED INTO THE STORE and reaches ZERO readers
detail: Per the ruling, four trials' published reports were recovered from evidence/2026-08-19-batch1/pericarditis_publication_extraction.json into inputs.trials[].published_report_read -- citation, PMID, DOI, source_read, and population, comparator and primary outcome in the paper's own words with the location of each quote. MEASURED AT SERVED BYTES: 0 of 4 trials have ANY of those values on the page. The generator renders no such field. The page grew 1,039 bytes and none of it is the evidence. TWO THINGS THIS ALSO SETTLED: (1) `per_trial` is a POOL-INPUT structure, not an evidence table -- 176 of 182 rows corpus-wide carry trial_id/measure/point/ci on a common scale, and the builder REFUSED my incommensurable rows with KeyError: 'trial_id'. The refusal was correct: populating it would have manufactured the commensurability the extraction refutes. So per_trial is left empty with the reason recorded in the object. (2) The display therefore needs a renderer for published_report_read, which lives in a CLASS-WIDE file.

This is the worked example: four properly cited trials, each primary in its own words, and an explicit statement that they cannot be combined. It is what the 23 verdict-only pages should look like -- but it needs one renderer before any of it is visible.

title: rerun_bookkeeping_with_lead_ins_2026_08_23.py destroys the PREVIOUS quarantine before making the new one
detail: Line 138-141, under the comment '2 QUARANTINE, BEFORE ANY WRITE': if os.path.isdir(QUAR): shutil.rmtree(QUAR); os.makedirs(QUAR). The script's own docstring says it quarantines 'to a FILE ON DISK rather than a git stash -- something that can be' recovered. A second invocation therefore deletes the previous run's safety copy BEFORE creating the replacement. It verifies the new quarantine (n_q = len(os.listdir(QUAR))) and never checks what it removed. Found by scripts/lint_destructive_without_asserted_backup.py, which is the only finding in 1,163 scripts.
ask: Low severity -- git holds the history -- but it is the exact class the lint exists for, in the one place designed to be a backup. Whoever owns that script should decide: timestamp the quarantine, or assert the old one is redundant before removing it.

title: The GRADE 'pending' resolver is CORRECT. The proposed class-wide fix would publish certainty ratings whose risk-of-bias domain is contested, on 19 indexed pages.
what_the_finding_said: sotagliflozin-hf records low certainty for all 3/3 outcomes and its bookkeeping says 'grade per pool' is held, while the class-wide resolver renders all three as PENDING. Proposed fix: publish the recorded level.
why_it_is_refuted: _rob_state(sotagliflozin-hf) computes dual=true, adjudicated=false, n_assessors=2, results_assessed=4, outcomes_assessed=[hfcv_first, hfcv_total]. TWO ASSESSORS READ EVERY CONTRIBUTING RESULT AND NOBODY ADJUDICATED THE DISAGREEMENT. That is read from the object, not assumed.
hfcv_total and hfcv_first are assessed but dual-unadjudicated, so their risk-of-bias domain has no final judgement.

mace3_first is NOT IN outcomes_assessed AT ALL -- the assessment covers two other outcomes. Its certainty would rest on a risk-of-bias domain with no assessment of that outcome anywhere on the object.
Each outcome's stored grade.certainty is 'low', DERIVED WITH a risk-of-bias domain as one of its five inputs. Publishing the level asserts that derivation is settled when its input is not.

The resolver's own comment states the ordering deliberately: 'PENDING outranks RATED, and only RATED ... it is precisely the case where a level EXISTS and may not yet be published.' It is a designed refusal, not an oversight.
what_the_real_defect_is: The BOOKKEEPING claim overstates. 'Of the four properties this project requires of a completed topic, 4 are held (comparison denominator, GRADE PER POOL, model output verbatim, rob per result)' -- the object holds a grade LEVEL, but a level whose risk-of-bias input is unresolved is not a published per-pool GRADE. The page is right and the bookkeeping sentence is the thing to correct.
abort_condition_met: Mahmood's stated abort condition was 'any page whose certainty level changes in a direction you cannot derive from its own stored fields'. This change would move 19 indexed pages from PENDING to a published level, and the stored fields say the risk-of-bias domain behind that level is contested. It met the abort condition BEFORE the first page was touched.
also_would_have_broken: gepotidacin is FROZEN and is 1 of the 20 behaviour pages. The fix as proposed had no exclusion for it.
cost_if_i_am_wrong: If the resolver really is over-cautious, 19 indexed pages continue to show PENDING with a stated reason instead of a LOW rating -- a page that under-claims with an explanation. If I am right and it had landed, 19 indexed pages would publish a certainty rating resting on an unadjudicated risk-of-bias domain, and one on an outcome never assessed. The asymmetry is why this is refused rather than staged.
ask: Confirm. If you want the levels published anyway, that is a methodological ruling about whether a GRADE certainty may be shown while its RoB domain is unadjudicated -- not a code fix, and it needs to be yours.
